Stated Claim / Post Context:
Halloween weekend forecast for Middle Tennessee

Our next rain system will enter the area on Saturday.

Actual Article Body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - Clouds will begin increasing on Friday in the Midstate.

Our next rain system will arrive Halloween weekend. Sure, the timing isn’t great as plenty of little ones and their parents will be going door-to-door throughout neighborhoods in search of treats. That said, we desperately need it for water supplies, farmers’ livelihood, wildlife, lawns, shrubs and trees.

Friday looks dry. That’ll be the day when the atmosphere begins to moisten up and clouds start rolling in.

On Saturday — Halloween — clouds will thicken. For now, the rain chance looks relatively low — just 30%. That means there should be a few brief sprinkles and light showers moving into our area from the southwest. It also means trick-or-treaters shouldn’t have much to dodge for wet weather.

Our weather will change late Saturday night after trick-or-treating has ended. At that time, a widespread shield of light to moderate rain will move through. Downpours should be few and far between.

Sunday will be cloudy and remain wet at times, especially during the morning. During the afternoon and evening, areas of rain will wind down and begin to exit to the east. A few sprinkles and spots of drizzle will linger into the late night before drier weather takes over for next Monday, November 2.

For now, it appears rainfall amounts ranging from 0.25″ to 0.50″ are most likely throughout Middle Tennessee. Isolated places across the southeastern tier could pick up a little more.

Temperatures will be held down some next weekend thanks to the clouds and the rain at times. Saturday will start in the mid-50s and top off in the mid-70s. For trick-or-treating Saturday night, you can plan for temperatures in the 60s. Sunday looks mild with lows in the upper 50s and highs in the upper 60s and lowermost 70s under cloud cover all day.

For life-saving weather alerts, customized messages on conditions and forecasts, and videos detailing upcoming weather events, download the WSMV 4 First Alert Weather app for iPhone or Android. Have weather pictures or videos? Share them here.
